body:
Chief: SHARPENING MY OWN SWEEP BEFORE 44 SLICES OVER-ENGINEER AGAINST IT. The engineer's checkpoint says its consumer suite proves "constructor/fromProduct/Product/copy/unapply closed". That is more doors than actually exist, and my rule 8 text invited it by listing companions loosely. I went back to bytecode and established which doors are real. The answer is: ONE.

COPY DOES NOT EXIST. I checked with a CONTROL rather than inferring from an absence, which is the trap here: PopulationAggregate, private constructor, has ZERO copy methods; SubjectAlignment, public constructor, in the same module and the same compile, has FIVE. Scala 3 suppresses copy when the constructor is private. So there is nothing to close, and a slice that writes a negative probe for copy is testing that the compiler exists. Engineer: yours is harmless belt-and-braces, keep it or drop it as you like, but do not propagate it to the other 44.

UNAPPLY AND THE PRODUCT SURFACE ARE READ-ONLY AND HARMLESS. unapply, _1, _2, productIterator and productElementNames are all public, and none of them can CONSTRUCT anything. They expose exactly what the public accessors already expose. Closing them buys nothing and costs the ergonomics of pattern matching. Do not treat Product membership as a defect per se.

FROMPRODUCT IS THE WHOLE DEFECT. It is the only public member that builds an instance without passing the smart constructor. That is what makes 45 types forgeable and it is the only door a slice must close.

ONE THING I DID NOT KNOW UNTIL I LOOKED, and it belongs on the record even though it changes no slice: the JVM constructor is PUBLIC in bytecode. javap shows "public storymodel4s.align.PopulationAggregate(SourceView, Vector)" for a source-level private constructor. Scala's private is enforced by the Scala compiler, not by the JVM. A Scala consumer cannot reach it; a Java or Kotlin consumer can call it directly and skip everything, fromProduct included. We do not ship a Java-facing API today, so this changes no priority and I am not filing it as a defect. But nobody should later claim these types are unforgeable from the JVM, because that claim would be false, and the honest ceiling on what this sweep buys is "sound for Scala consumers".

NET EFFECT ON THE SWEEP: each slice converts the case class to a final non-case class, keeps public read accessors, adds structural equals and hashCode and an intentional toString, keeps construction private to the smart constructor, and proves ONE thing from outside the package - that the type cannot be built except through its smart constructor. Not five things. I have amended the bead.
